title: fix: cap Ling 3.1 Flash at 8 RPM per user
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Caps Ling 3.1 Flash at 8 RPM per authenticated user, shared across the user's API keys and IPs.
- Uses the existing token bucket and returns 429 with Retry-After when exhausted. Both hidden fallback routes inherit the cap.

| Model | Action | Change | Before | After | Effective |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `inclusionai/ling-3.1-flash` | UPDATE | Per-user request limit | Uncapped | 8 RPM | On production deployment (not live yet) |

Validation: 58 focused rate-limit/fallback tests, Gen typecheck, Biome, and diff checks pass.

gist.headline: One bucket for every key
gist.blurb: Ling 3.1 Flash gets one shared request bucket per user. Extra keys and fallback routes still lead to the same garden gate.
gist.summary: Ling 3.1 Flash changes from uncapped to 8 requests per minute per authenticated user, shared across API keys and IPs; both hidden fallback routes inherit the limit.
gist.impact: Users can make 8 Ling 3.1 Flash requests per minute across their keys and IPs, with a 429 response and Retry-After header when the shared bucket is empty.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a single watering can marked “8 / MIN” serving several paths to one Ling 3.1 Flash code-plant. Polli tends the plant while a friendly CRT robot watches the shared counter; the converging paths represent API keys, IPs, and fallback routes without implying separate allowances.
